sources.entry: Web Servers and Reverse Proxies. A web server is a piece of software and underlying hardware that accepts requests via HTTP (the network protocol created to distribute web content) or its secure variant HTTPS. summary.name: Web server (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article explaining what web server software is, how it handles HTTP/HTTPS requests, and the history and technical workings of web servers.
use_cases: understanding how web servers process requests
learning the history of web server software
studying URL mapping and path translation
background reading on HTTP server design
summary.what_it_does: This is an encyclopedia article, not a software product. It describes a web server as software and hardware that accepts HTTP or HTTPS requests and returns content or errors. It covers static versus dynamic content, the typical tasks a server performs when handling a request, such as URL normalization, mapping, and path translation, and common features like logging, virtual hosting, caching, and bandwidth throttling. It also traces the history of web servers from CERN httpd and NCSA httpd through Apache, IIS, Nginx, and the adoption of HTTP/2.
notable: Historical timeline from CERN httpd (1990s) through Apache, IIS, and Nginx
Step-by-step explanation of how a server processes an HTTP request
Worked examples of URL path translation to file system paths
caveats: Encyclopedia article, so it does not describe a single downloadable tool
Some sections are flagged as needing more citations or updates
